catalog_rules: Reuse an existing tactic ID when objective, mechanism, artifacts, acceptance boundary, verification and reassessment are materially the same.
Criterion and anti-pattern objects contain generated reverse references only.
Runtime activation requires a locked eligible finding and contextual eligibility evaluation.
Tactic completion never changes finding state and never overrides a hard gate.
Cross-category reuse extends exact finding mappings; it does not create a second ID for the same remediation mechanism.

tactics.title: Establish AI-specific threat model and attack-surface baseline
tactics.objective: Create a system-specific, lifecycle-aware model of assets, threat actors, AI-specific attack paths, consequences, existing controls and residual risk.
activities: Define system assets, trust boundaries, untrusted inputs, external services, tools, data stores and privileged effects.
Select applicable predictive, generative, retrieval and agentic attack modules; record excluded modules with rationale.
Model attacker goals, capabilities and paths, including poisoning, evasion, privacy/confidentiality, misuse and prompt-injection paths where applicable.
Map each material path to preventive, detective, responsive and recovery controls and an accountable owner.
Define risk-based acceptance thresholds and adversarial test obligations for the target lifecycle transition.
acceptance_criteria: The complete deployed system, not only the model, is in scope.
All reachable untrusted-input and privileged-effect paths are represented or explicitly excluded with rationale.
Each material path has an owner, planned control and verification method.
Security and system owners approve the baseline for the target stage.
verification: Trace sample attack paths from source to protected asset
Reconcile model against current component and data-flow inventories
do_not_use_when: The need is solely a general network or identity architecture redesign already governed under D1; link rather than duplicate that work.

tactics.title: Enforce untrusted AI output and downstream execution boundaries
tactics.objective: Ensure generated output is treated as untrusted data and cannot become code, commands, markup, policy or privileged action without deterministic validation and constrained execution.
activities: Inventory every interpreter, renderer, query builder, workflow engine and service that consumes model output.
Define typed schemas and allowlisted operations; reject unexpected fields, destinations, commands and encodings.
Apply context-appropriate escaping, parameterization, sandboxing and output encoding.
Separate suggestion generation from authorization and execution; require deterministic policy checks and human approval where consequence requires it.
Add negative tests for injection, unsafe rendering, path/URL manipulation, command generation and cross-context contamination.
acceptance_criteria: No security-relevant consumer executes free-form model output directly.
Invalid or unauthorized outputs fail closed and create observable events.
Representative injection and unsafe-output tests meet approved thresholds.
Bypass and fallback paths are included in testing.
verification: Trace rejected and approved actions in telemetry
do_not_use_when: The system produces isolated text with no renderer, interpreter, retrieval write-back, external action or consequential decision path; record the narrower applicable controls instead.

tactics.title: Operationalize AI-security monitoring and incident response
tactics.objective: Detect, triage, contain, learn from and recover from AI-specific attacks and control failures in the intended operating context.
activities: Define AI-specific security events, detection signals and severity thresholds without logging unnecessary sensitive content.
Capture model, prompt, retrieval, tool, policy, decision and version identifiers needed for investigation.
Create containment actions such as tool disablement, route isolation, credential revocation, model rollback and safe-mode operation.
Integrate events into incident response, vulnerability disclosure, post-incident reassessment and regression testing.
Exercise at least one representative AI attack and one control-failure scenario before the target production transition.
acceptance_criteria: Material AI attack paths have observable indicators and accountable responders.
Containment actions can be executed within the approved response objective.
An exercise demonstrates triage, containment, evidence preservation and reassessment.
Monitoring design respects privacy, confidentiality and retention requirements.
do_not_use_when: The system is an isolated, non-operational experiment with no live users, sensitive data or external effects; define pre-production logging and future activation criteria instead.

tactics.title: Enforce deterministic tool input and action validation
tactics.objective: Prevent model-selected tools, arguments and actions from exceeding approved identity, data, destination and consequence boundaries.
activities: Define per-tool typed contracts, caller identity, allowed resources, destinations, rates and read/write effects.
Validate arguments, authorization and business preconditions outside the model before each action.
Require human approval or two-step commit for irreversible, external or high-impact actions.
Enforce budgets, rate limits, idempotency, rollback and loop detection.
Test unauthorized tools, malformed arguments, privilege escalation, cross-tenant access, recursive calls and approval bypass.
acceptance_criteria: Model output alone cannot authorize a tool or privileged action.
Every action is bound to an authenticated principal and scoped authorization decision.
Negative tests prove denial of representative unauthorized and malformed actions.
Consequential actions are reversible or require an approved human decision boundary.
do_not_use_when: The identified issue is excessive authority assignment rather than adversarial validation; coordinate with C3 and reuse this tactic only for the enforcement portion.

tactics.title: Establish retrieval and untrusted-content trust boundaries
tactics.objective: Prevent retrieved, uploaded, browsed or third-party content from becoming trusted instructions or contaminating privileged context and downstream actions.
activities: Classify retrieval and content sources by trust, ownership, tenant, freshness and instruction risk.
Separate system instructions, user intent, retrieved evidence and external content in the execution design.
Restrict retrieval scope, connectors, URLs, file types, recursion and write-back; preserve source provenance.
Detect or neutralize instruction-like content where feasible, while treating detection as defense in depth rather than a security boundary.
Test indirect prompt injection, poisoned documents, cross-tenant retrieval, hidden instructions and malicious links across bypass paths.
acceptance_criteria: Untrusted content cannot redefine system authority or bypass deterministic controls.
Retrieval is tenant-, purpose- and source-scoped with traceable provenance.
Representative indirect-injection and poisoned-content tests meet approved thresholds.
Fallback, caching, browsing and ingestion paths are covered.
do_not_use_when: The system has no retrieval, browsing, upload, external-content or memory path; record not applicable with evidence.

tactics.title: Execute AI-specific adversarial evaluation and regression assurance
tactics.objective: Demonstrate, within a defined scope and confidence boundary, how the complete AI system behaves under representative malicious and abusive conditions.
activities: Derive test cases from the approved threat model and select only applicable attack modules.
Cover direct and indirect prompt injection, unsafe output handling, retrieval poisoning, tool abuse and other predictive/generative attack classes that apply.
Define environments, versions, attack success criteria, severity, coverage, stopping rules and reproducibility requirements.
Execute tests against the complete system, including fallbacks, secondary paths and realistic privileges; preserve evidence.
Remediate, retest, baseline residual limitations and convert material cases into release-blocking regression tests.
acceptance_criteria: Tests trace to applicable threat-model paths and current system versions.
Attack success criteria and severity are defined before execution.
Material failures are remediated or explicitly escalated; retest evidence is preserved.
Critical cases become automated or repeatable regression tests and are rerun after material change.
A TESTED_ABSENT anti-pattern conclusion states the exact tested scope and does not imply universal immunity.
verification: Independent review of plan and evidence
Reproduction of a sample of passing and failing cases
Regression execution in the release pipeline
do_not_use_when: A generic vulnerability scan is the only planned method; it does not establish AI-specific adversarial resilience.
